question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=2x{e}^{y},\,x\ge 0,\,y\le -{x}^{2}.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,\,y\le -{x}^{2}\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/1bc2723ca6b5ee5af27bb6f9cb8e3462dde99a4686542b3f8c273a4148ede595.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $y\le 0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{-y}}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{-y}}x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{e}^{y}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{-y}} \\  & =[{x}^{2}{e}^{y}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{-y}} \\  & =[{(\sqrt{-y})}^{2}\cdot {e}^{y}-{0}^{2}\cdot {e}^{y}] \\  & =-y{e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}-y{e}^{y}, & y\le 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
